newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares hit by selling in cements, mills.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares hit by selling in cements, mills.

text.p: Egyptian shares touched another five-month low on Monday as selling hit most of the dominant sectors -- cements, flour mills and the popular banks.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell 1.63 points to 348.37, its lowest since January 21. Turnover was 39.69 million pounds ($11.69 million), slightly below average.
Prices have been moving downwards since early in the month and brokers say the market needs more privatisation and improvements in the exchange systems to reverse the trend.

But they also say that at these levels there are plenty of bargains. "The market is overreacting. First it was overpriced and now it is underpriced. It's going from one extreme to another," said Mohamed Abdulla of brokers Intercapital.
The big four cement companies bore the brunt of Monday's sell-off, slumping across the board in volume that accounted for about one fifth of the day's total.
Helwan Portland Cement lost 0.14 to close at 71.21 pounds, Amriyah Cement dropped 0.98 to 81.02 and Suez Cement closed 0.59 down at 66.10.

Two big banks were also very active but were affected by the the same downward trend. Commercial International Bank/CIB shed 0.44 to 71.5 and Misr International Bank/MIBank lost 12.50 to close at 557.5.
Mills, a traditional barometer of market sentiment, were all lower in relatively small volumes, led downwards by Upper Egypt Flour Mills, which slipped 0.29 to 77.61.
But General Silos and Storage, which usually tracks the milling sector, recovered some of its recent losses. It ended 1.00 pound up at 91.00 in some large-transaction trade.

"The bourse is boring, foreign investors are bored and disappointed with the pace of the privatisation programme. They don't want to trade the same stocks, the market needs broadening," said Patrick George, a Middle East analyst at London-based securities house HSBC James Capel.
But he added: "Egypt is still a favourite among emerging markets. We recommend this market and now it's attractive."
The index for openly traded firms fell to 477.08 from 479.71 points on Sunday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also slipped to 257.65 from 258.75.
Of the 95 shares traded, 31 rose, 34 fell while 30 ended unchanged.
